ma_douglas_state_forest.blurb: Douglas State Forest is a large wooded tract in the town of Douglas, in south-central Massachusetts right against the Connecticut and Rhode Island lines, built around Wallum Lake and a cedar swamp. Climbing here is overwhelmingly bouldering, with only a scattering of trad and top-rope lines. Problems run from very easy to very hard, with the bulk between V1 and V5 and a tail up to V7 and beyond. Boulderfields lie west of the lake, spread out but mostly within a ten-minute walk. Far North holds most of the roped climbing along with some of the harder problems, while Mine Brook Boulders and the Streeter area add more variety. Rock quality is generally good.

or_carver_bouldering.blurb: Carver is a hillside boulder field below a small cliff, about twenty minutes from downtown Portland near Gresham. It is bouldering only, with a wide spread of difficulty: plenty of easy problems from V0 to V2, a solid core around V3 and V4, and a thin tail of hard testpieces reaching into the double digits. Most of the problems are found in the Main Forest, with the Bonzai Boulders as the next largest cluster and smaller groups such as the James Dean Boulders. Expect a varied area where beginners and strong boulderers both find a day's worth of climbing.

wi_group_camps.blurb: Group Camps lies in the northern part of Governor Dodge State Park, near Dodgeville and roughly an hour west of Madison. Giant sandstone boulders scattered through the woods make up most of the climbing, and the largest cluster sits at Group Camp B, on a hilltop with a prominent ridge that has problems on both sides. Most problems are V0 to V4, with a steady supply of harder ones up to V8. Qual Wall adds bolted sport routes from about 5.8 to 5.12, and there are a few trad and top-rope lines. The stone is quite good in places but soft or crumbly elsewhere, so treat it gently. It is a lower-key scene than nearby Devil's Lake.

az_san_francisco_peaks.blurb: The San Francisco Peaks are a volcanic range rising above Flagstaff in northern Arizona, with a handful of small crags on their flanks. Sport climbing dominates, backed by a meaningful amount of trad, and almost everything falls between 5.9 and 5.13 with the heart of it at 5.10 to 5.12. Hobo Jungle is the busiest and most varied wall, on dacite, with a few moderates for newer leaders among its many 5.11s. Secret Garden is a quieter spot where steep, pumpy 5.10s sit beside 5.12s, while Peaks Crag sits in a canyon on the south side and is said to shine in the fall. Ghost Town is remote and rarely visited.

co_garden_of_the_gods.blurb: Garden of the Gods is a compact city park in Colorado Springs, near Manitou Springs, where tilted red, pink and white sandstone fins stand against the plains at the foot of the mountains. Climbing is a mix of bouldering, sport and trad in nearly equal measure, climbable year-round. Routes run from about 5.4 to 5.13, with most in the 5.8 to 5.11 band, and bouldering is mostly V0 to V4 with a few much harder problems. The stone is soft, porous and fragile, so quality varies from formation to formation and old hardware deserves suspicion. Main areas include the Snake Pit, North and South Gateway Rocks, and Kindergarten Rock.

sc_big_rock_mountain.blurb: Big Rock Mountain sits near Pickens in the upstate of South Carolina, a scatter of granite pinnacles, slabs and boulderfields that has been compared to a small Joshua Tree. Trad leads the roped climbing, with sport routes and a large block of bouldering alongside, from V0 to a few V8s. Most roped lines are 5.8 to 5.12, often under 80 feet, with a few two-pitch outings. Main Wall, X-Wall and Arch Wall are the biggest cliffs, and the Big Rock Boulders hold the most problems. Cliffs face south and catch the sun, making it mainly a fall, winter and spring destination; summer brings thick growth and insects. Rock drains quickly after rain.
